root.label: pair, tuple, tuple protocol
root.note: Structs with numbered members, plus the protocol that lets any type behave like one.

children.label: Construction
children.note: Element-wise, converting and piecewise ways to build pairs and tuples.

children.label: Conditional explicit
children.note: The element-wise constructor is explicit only when some element conversion is explicit.

children.label: Deduction
children.note: tuple t{1, 2.5} deduces element types, and a single tuple argument is copied, not nested.

children.label: Piecewise
children.note: piecewise_construct with forward_as_tuple builds each member in place, as map::emplace needs.

children.label: Tuples of references
children.note: A bundle of aliases that supports multiple assignment.

children.label: make_tuple
children.note: Decays and copies arguments, and unwraps reference_wrapper into references.

children.label: tie
children.note: Makes a tuple of lvalue references, so assigning to it assigns the variables.

children.label: forward_as_tuple
children.note: Forwarding references with no copies; storing the result can dangle.

children.label: Assignment through
children.note: Assigning tuples of references assigns the referents; C++23 adds const assignment for proxies.

children.label: std::ignore
children.note: Accepts any assignment and discards it, to skip a position in tie.

children.label: Comparison
children.note: Lexicographic ordering with a derived comparison category.

children.label: Lexicographic
children.note: The first differing element decides; sizes must match.

children.label: Spaceship category
children.note: The result is the weakest category of the elements, so a double gives partial_ordering.

children.label: Tuple algorithms
children.note: Functions that consume or combine tuple-like values.

children.label: apply
children.note: Calls a function with the elements of a tuple-like object as arguments.

children.label: make_from_tuple
children.note: Constructs a T from the elements of a tuple-like object.

children.label: tuple_cat
children.note: Flattens one level, concatenating tuples, pairs and arrays into one tuple.

children.label: Tuple protocol
children.note: tuple_size, tuple_element and get make any type tuple-like.

children.label: Structured bindings
children.note: Bindings use the protocol whenever tuple_size is complete, before the struct rule.

children.label: tuple-like in C++23
children.note: array, pair, tuple and subrange qualify, and tuple and pair convert from any of them.

children.label: Practice
children.note: Where tuples help and where a named struct is better.

children.label: No layout guarantee
children.note: Member order and padding are unspecified, so never reinterpret a tuple.

children.label: Prefer a struct
children.note: Once fields cross an interface, names beat first and second.
